label: Azetidine
pka_note: pKaH ~11.1; dependent on substitution on N

label: Piperidine
pka_note: pKaH ~11.1; dependent on substitution on N

label: Morpholine
pka_note: pKaH ~8.4; dependent on substitution on N

label: Pyrrolidine
pka_note: pKaH ~11.3; dependent on substitution on N

label: Pyrrole
pka_note: N lone pair is part of the aromatic sextet — non-basic

label: Furan
pka_note: O lone pair delocalized into the ring — non-basic

label: Indole
pka_note: N-H weakly acidic (pKa ~17); ring N non-basic

label: Purine (xanthine/guanine core)
pka_note: ring N basic (e.g. adenine pKaH ~4.2); N-H also weakly acidic

label: Oxazolidinone
pka_note: cyclic carbamate — non-ionizable at physiological pH

label: beta-Lactam
pka_note: cyclic amide — non-ionizable at physiological pH

label: Urea
pka_note: very weakly basic (pKaH ~0.1) — treated as non-ionizable

label: Guanidine
pka_note: pKaH ~13.6 — strongest common organic base, protonated at all physiological pH

label: Hydrazide/hydrazine
pka_note: hydrazine pKaH ~8; hydrazides are much weaker bases

label: Primary amine
pka_note: pKaH ~9-11 (aliphatic); anilines weaker, ~4-5. Undergoes oxidative deamination (MAO/CYP) to an aldehyde.

label: Secondary amine
pka_note: pKaH ~10-11 (aliphatic); anilines weaker. N-dealkylation is a common CYP metabolic route.

label: Tertiary amine
pka_note: pKaH ~9-10 (aliphatic, often slightly lower); anilines weaker. N-dealkylation or N-oxidation are common CYP routes.

label: Primary alcohol
pka_note: pKa ~16-18 (non-ionizable). Oxidizes metabolically to an aldehyde, then a carboxylic acid.

label: Secondary alcohol
pka_note: pKa ~16-18 (non-ionizable). Oxidizes metabolically to a ketone.

label: Tertiary alcohol
pka_note: pKa ~16-18 (non-ionizable). No C-H on the carbinol carbon, so it resists metabolic oxidation; typically cleared by glucuronidation instead.

label: Sulfoxide
pka_note: very weakly basic on O — treated as non-ionizable

label: Sulfonic acid
pka_note: pKa ~ -2 to 1 (very strong acid, essentially always ionized at physiological pH)

label: Sulfate ester
pka_note: pKa ~ -3 to 1 (very strong acid); common phase II metabolic conjugate (sulfation)

label: Quaternary amine
pka_note: Permanently charged, not pH-dependent — always ionized regardless of pH. Not metabolized by CYP N-dealkylation the way tertiary amines are.

label: Azide
pka_note: Non-ionizable; the azide group itself is a weak base at the terminal N but not relevant at physiological pH.

label: N-oxide
pka_note: Permanently charged like a quaternary amine, but reversible: N-oxides are commonly reduced back to the parent tertiary amine metabolically (e.g. by CYP or gut flora), unlike a true quaternary ammonium salt.
